AlertingStatusOut.description:
OD-19's gap, made visible.

`state` is `unconfigured` when alerting is on and no destination is set — an
operator reading `/readyz` can see that alerts are being dropped instead of
discovering it during an incident.
AlertingStatusOut.title: AlertingStatusOut

AssignCounterRequest.description:
`null` detaches the computer from every counter.

A sub-resource carrying one field rather than a general `PUT /admin/devices/{id}`:
this is the only device column an administrator may set here, and a wider body would
let a counter assignment also rewrite a device's label, branch or revocation state.
AssignCounterRequest.title: AssignCounterRequest

CatalogDeltaOut.description:
⚠️ `cost_price` is **never** present, regardless of permission: a stolen counter
machine must not carry the shop's margins (`SECURITY.md §11`).
CatalogDeltaOut.title: CatalogDeltaOut

CreditCustomerOut.description:
Every aggregate is **server-computed**; the client never sums these
(FR-RPT-030, ADR-032).
CreditCustomerOut.title: CreditCustomerOut

DailySalesOut.description: `GET /reports/daily-sales` — the one report a screen renders field by field.
DailySalesOut.title: DailySalesOut

DraftPreviewTotalsOut.description:
Always advisory. The server recomputes everything at finalisation
(FR-DRAFT-011).
DraftPreviewTotalsOut.title: DraftPreviewTotalsOut

FinalizeOut.description: The `201` from `POST /sales:finalize` — cash and credit alike (ADR-033).
FinalizeOut.title: FinalizeOut

ImportReportOut.description: FR-IMP-009. Carries the skipped rows and their reasons, not just the counts.
ImportReportOut.title: ImportReportOut

ImportUploadOut.description:
`202` from `POST /imports`.

`duplicate_of_job_id` is present and null on a normal upload rather than omitted:
unlike `cost_price`, its absence carries no permission meaning, and a client
checking `=== null` is clearer than one checking `in`.
ImportUploadOut.title: ImportUploadOut

InvoiceOut.description:
One shape, returned by `POST /sales:finalize` **and** `GET /invoices/{id}`.

Built by a single serialiser (`api/v1/serialize.py`), because the confirmation card
and the Daily Bills detail describe the same bill.
InvoiceOut.title: InvoiceOut

MoneyPolicyOut.description: Published so the client never hardcodes a rounding or whole-rupee rule.
MoneyPolicyOut.title: MoneyPolicyOut

PaymentHistoryOut.description:
One row of `GET /payments`.

Declared for M25: the customer screen shows a payment history, and an undeclared
response left the client stringifying `unknown` values — which ESLint correctly
refused, because `String(someObject)` yields `[object Object]` on a screen showing
money.
PaymentHistoryOut.title: PaymentHistoryOut

PrintBusinessOut.description: Empty optional fields print nothing — **never a placeholder** (FR-PRINT-016).
PrintBusinessOut.title: PrintBusinessOut

PrintPayloadOut.description:
⚠️ Carries **no invoice number** of any kind (OD-3, T3-06).

`document_title` comes from the server only and is `ESTIMATE` for cash and credit
alike until the FR-TAX-003 gate passes (OD-24, FR-PRINT-021).
PrintPayloadOut.title: PrintPayloadOut

ReportOut.description:
The common report envelope (`API-SPECIFICATION.md §3.11`).

⚠️ The **only** permissive model in this module. Each report spreads its own figures
at the top level — `daily-sales` has `gross`/`net`/`by_day`, `stock-position` has
`rows` — so `extra="forbid"` would make one model impossible. The envelope is what
every report shares and what the client relies on; the per-report figures are typed
where a screen renders them field by field (`DailySalesOut`).
ReportOut.title: ReportOut

SaleHeaderIn.description: Optional for **both** sale types, and persisted when present (FR-CREDIT-012).
SaleHeaderIn.title: SaleHeaderIn

get.description:
The customer directory, newest first.

Added because there was no way to list customers at all. `GET /customers/search`
needs a term, and the only other read-many is `GET /credit/customers`, which
inner-joins credit invoices — it answers "who owes us money" and is the top of the
Credit Bills view. The Customers screen was reading from it, so a customer with no
credit invoice could not be seen or found there, and one created through
`Add a customer` appeared to vanish.

Declared before `/{customer_id}` because FastAPI matches in declaration order and
`""` would otherwise be swallowed by the path-parameter route.

`cursor` is opaque: the previous page's last `created_at` as epoch microseconds.
Deliberately **not** ISO-8601 — an ISO timestamp with an offset contains a `+`, which
a query string decodes as a space, so a caller who pasted `next_cursor` straight into
a URL got a 422. Microseconds match PostgreSQL's `timestamptz` precision, sort as an
integer, and need no escaping.

Keyset, not offset: a directory that grows while someone pages through it must not
skip or repeat a row.

`202`, not `201`: the job exists but has not been read yet. The client polls

Returns every row with its result and reason — including the skipped ones, which are

code matched nothing" is a report that hides exactly what the reader needs.

Record one human decision (FR-IMP-007).

The body is a plain dict rather than a model because it carries exactly two
optional keys and a strict model here would add a schema for `{decision,
matched_product_id}` that says nothing the enum does not.

schema.title: Response Decide Import Row Api V1 Imports  Job Id  Rows  Row Id  Patch

post.description:
One decision for every pending row in a status.

Not in the original route list, and added for a reason that only shows up with a
real file: a supplier price list of 400 unstocked parts produces 400 `new_product`
rows, and a reviewer forced to click each one will stop reading by row 20. A
decision about a whole category is a judgement someone can actually hold in mind.

schema.title: Response Decide All Import Rows Api V1 Imports  Job Id  Rows Decide All Post

post.description:
Apply the accepted rows in one transaction (FR-IMP-008).

`idempotency_key` is required by the API contract and accepted here; the job's own
terminal `applied` state is what actually prevents a second application, which is
the stronger guarantee — it holds even for a client that generates a fresh key.

post.description: Cancel a job that has not been applied (FR-IMP-005).

schema.title: Response Cancel Import Api V1 Imports  Job Id  Cancel Post

A reasoned, audited correction. `Idempotency-Key` is required so a retried
adjustment cannot be applied twice.

Also carries T3-04's numbering check: per series, `max(sequence_number) + 1` must

The caller's business's unread notices.

No specific permission: these are notices about the business the caller is already

deployment's monitoring posture, which is an operator's concern, and the destination
hint — even reduced to scheme and host — is infrastructure detail a counter hand has
no reason to see.

Atomically finalise a cash or credit sale.

Everything between BEGIN and COMMIT either all happens or none of it does

draft's finalised state, the audit row and the outbox event. Stock is deducted
**exactly once**.
